overview: Kent was already a kingdom when Augustine arrived in 597. Canterbury connects its royal court, continental contacts and early institutions of Christian learning.

items.text: King Aethelberht welcomed Augustine and granted the missionaries land near Canterbury. His Frankish wife Bertha already worshipped at St Martin's.
The abbey was probably founded in 598. Its precinct included religious buildings and burial grounds alongside vineyards, orchards and gardens.
The monastery developed a school that attracted students from afar.
Its scriptorium became an influential centre of book production; this institutional history continued after Kent's early royal phase.

sources.title: English Heritage: History of St Augustine's Abbey
